research_question: How much warmer was Earth in 2024 than the 1951–1980 average, and how fast has it been warming since 1975?
intro: Scientists rarely report Earth's absolute temperature. They report an anomaly: how much warmer or cooler a period was compared with a fixed reference period (the baseline).
NASA's GISTEMP v4 combines land station and sea-surface measurements into a single global monthly anomaly relative to 1951–1980. NASA reported 2024 as 1.28 °C above that baseline.
In this mission you will rebuild that headline number from the monthly data yourself, measure the warming trend, and then test whether your method works on a dataset you have never seen.

concepts.def: The difference between a measured temperature and the average over a baseline period. Positive = warmer than the baseline.
The reference period used to compute anomalies. GISTEMP uses 1951–1980. Different datasets may use different baselines, so their anomaly values are not directly comparable.
The average of the 12 monthly values of a calendar year (January–December).
The slope of the straight line that best fits the data by ordinary least squares (OLS). Reported here in °C per decade (slope per year × 10).
Recomputing a published result from the same data and method. Here we reproduce part of the analysis (R1), not GISTEMP's full station processing.
The documented acceptable difference between your value and the reference calculation, which allows for honest rounding.

data_structure.description: One row per month. Columns: Year (e.g. 2024), Month (1–12), Anomaly_C (°C relative to 1951–1980).

quiz.q: A month has an anomaly of +0.50 °C in GISTEMP. What does that mean?
options: It was 0.50 °C warmer than the 1951–1980 average for that time
It was 0.50 °C warmer than the previous month
The thermometers had an error of 0.50 °C

feedback.0: An anomaly is not an absolute temperature — think about what it is compared with.
feedback.2: Anomalies are not month-to-month changes. What fixed reference is used?
feedback.3: Anomalies describe climate, not instrument error. Re-read the definition of baseline.

quiz.q: Which calculation gives the 2024 annual mean anomaly?
options: Sum of the 12 monthly anomalies of 2024
Average of the 12 monthly anomalies of 2024

feedback.0: A sum grows with the number of months. What statistic stays on the same scale as one month?
feedback.2: One month can be unusually warm or cold. Use the whole calendar year.
feedback.3: The question asks about one calendar year only.

quiz.q: Dataset A uses a 1951–1980 baseline and dataset B a different baseline. Which comparison is fair without adjustment?
options: Comparing their warming trends (°C per decade)

feedback.0: A baseline shift moves every value up or down by a constant — what quantity is unaffected by a constant shift?
feedback.2: Some quantities do not depend on the baseline. Which one?
feedback.3: Picking one month does not remove the baseline offset.

quiz.q: A trend of 0.02 °C per year equals how much per decade?

feedback.0: A decade is longer than a year — should the number get larger or smaller?
feedback.1: Per year and per decade are different units.
feedback.3: Check how many years are in a decade.

feedback.1: This is monthly, not quarterly, data.
